articles.desc: Bajaj Finance expects AUM to grow 26-27% in FY27 as it accelerates customer acquisition and loan disbursements. articles.desc: Kross shares surged following strong Q2 FY27 results, with revenue rising 80% and net profit climbing 143% year-on-year. EBITDA more than doubled, while margins improved. Robust commercial vehicle demand, capacity expansion and operational efficiencies supported growth, alongside increased institutional shareholding and the stock reaching a fresh 52-week high.

articles.title: Stock Market Holiday 2026: Are NSE, BSE closed on October 20 for Dussehra? Check remaining holidays for the year
articles.desc: The NSE and BSE will remain closed on October 20 for Dussehra. With 12 of the 16 scheduled stock market holidays for 2026 already passed, three more holidays remain after the October closure. These include Diwali-Balipratipada on November 10, Guru Nanak Jayanti on November 24 and Christmas on December 25.

articles.title: Global Market: China’s yuan hits four-year high as strong GDP data ease stimulus concerns
articles.desc: China’s yuan strengthened to a four-year high against the US dollar following stronger-than-expected third-quarter economic growth and improving retail sales. A weaker dollar and increased corporate currency conversions also supported gains. Investors now await Chinese policymakers’ signals on monetary policy, currency management and further economic stimulus measures.

articles.title: Ixigo shares rally 13% after travel platform reports all-time high profit
articles.desc: Ixigo shares jumped after the travel platform reported a record Q2 profit of Rs 63.42 crore, partly boosted by the sale of its stake in Freshbus. Gross transaction value rose 22% year-on-year to Rs 5,304.47 crore, while revenue grew 13% to Rs 320.96 crore and contribution margin increased 14% to Rs 124.86 crore.

articles.title: Global Market: Japan’s Nikkei falls 2% as tech selloff, rising oil prices fuel inflation fears
articles.desc: Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell as US technology stock losses and rising oil prices heightened inflation and interest rate concerns. Semiconductor stocks led declines, while defensive and value shares offered potential support. Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda highlighted inflation near the 2% target, keeping monetary policy expectations in focus.

articles.title: Sugar stocks Balrampur Chini, Bajaj Sugar, others crash up to 7% as centre stops diversion to ethanol
articles.desc: Sugar stocks dropped in early trading following the government's directive to cease sugar diversion for ethanol production. The decision impacts major sugar companies like Balrampur Chini Mills and Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar, which experienced a decline between 2% and 7%. This directive aims to enhance domestic sugar availability amidst rising prices. The government's action follows concerns about potential production shortfalls due to insufficient rainfall.

articles.title: Global Market: Japan bond yields fall as US tech selloff fuels safe-haven demand
articles.desc: Japanese government bond yields fell as a selloff in US technology stocks triggered demand for safer assets. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s pledge to control debt issuance also supported sentiment, while Bank of Japan rate expectations remained in focus.

articles.title: Exporters may be asked to monitor supply chains' indirect emissions
articles.desc: The Indian government is engaging in discussions about measuring Scope 3 emissions for exporters. This consideration arises as trade partners impose tighter green requirements globally. Current frameworks focus on direct emissions and exclude indirect ones, making compliance more complex. As a result, industries, especially MSMEs, may face compliance burdens if new requirements are implemented. Ultimately, the aim is to ensure that Indian exporters remain competitive in international markets.

articles.title: Farmers face 15% loss as poultry feed costs surge
articles.desc: Poultry farmers are currently experiencing losses of approximately 15% due to rising livestock feed costs. Key ingredients have seen price increases of up to 75%, affecting farmers' ability to cope. Dairy producers, particularly in drought-affected regions, struggle to source necessary fodder for their livestock. Feed manufacturers are also feeling the impact as higher prices reduce demand for their products.

articles.title: Global investors against use of judicial anti-avoidance rule by tax officials
articles.desc: International investors have raised concerns regarding the Indian Income-tax authorities' invocation of the judicial anti-avoidance rule. At a recent meeting, investors communicated their issues with the Central Board of Direct Taxes on this matter. The use of JAAR to deny relief on grandfathered shares contradicts prior regulations established by the CBDT. The standing of both GAAR and JAAR remains complex due to Supreme Court rulings.
